children: Australian shares hit a 5-week high on Friday, led by miners as softer-than-expected labour market data curbed expectations of a near-term interest rate hike and fuelled broad-based buying.

was up 1% at 8,809.80 points, as of 0025 GMT, after rising as much as 1.2% earlier in session, its highest since September 10. The benchmark was on course for its best week since mid-August, having gained 1% so far.
Data released on Thursday showed employment fell by the most in more than a year, prompting markets to revisit their bets on a rate hike.
Markets reduced the odds of a November hike to about 9% from 32% before the data. The chance of a December move fell to 28% from 56%.
